CA: Course to an altitude — a procedure where an aircraft follows a specified course until reaching a defined altitude, typically used in departure or arrival procedures.
CAT: Clear air turbulence — sudden severe turbulence occurring in cloudless air, often at high altitudes, associated with wind shear and jet streams.
CC: Cirrocumulus — a high-altitude cloud type appearing as small white patches or layers of rippled sheets, often indicating fair but cold weather.
CCO: Continuous climb operations — an operational procedure that allows aircraft to climb continuously to optimal cruise altitude without intermediate level-offs, reducing fuel burn and noise.
CD: Candela — the SI base unit of luminous intensity, used in aviation to specify the brightness of lighting systems such as runway edge lights and approach lights.
CDO: Continuous descent operations — an operational technique where arriving aircraft descend continuously from cruise altitude to the runway threshold with minimal thrust, reducing fuel consumption and noise.
CDR: Conditional route — a flexible air traffic services route that is available only under specified conditions, often used for military or seasonal airspace management.
CGL: Circling guidance light(s) — a lighting system that provides visual guidance to aircraft executing a circling approach to a runway not aligned with the instrument approach aid.
CHEM: Chemical — refers to the carriage, spillage, or hazard involving chemical substances, used in NOTAMs to notify of dangerous goods or contamination on movement areas.
CI: Cirrus — a high-altitude cloud type composed of ice crystals, appearing as white wispy filaments, often associated with fair weather but may indicate approaching frontal systems.
CIV: Civil — denoting civil aviation operations, aircraft, or facilities as distinct from military aviation.
CK: Check — used in NOTAMs and aviation communications to indicate a requirement to verify, inspect, or confirm a system, instrument, or condition.
CL: Centre line — the physical or visual centerline of a runway, taxiway, or airway, used as a reference for navigation and ground movement.
CLA: Clear type of ice formation — a transparent or translucent layer of ice that forms on aircraft surfaces, typically in freezing rain or high liquid water content conditions, posing aerodynamic risks.
CLBR: Calibration — the process of verifying and adjusting the accuracy of navigation aids, instruments, or airport equipment to ensure compliance with published standards.
CLD: Cloud — a visible mass of condensed water droplets or ice crystals suspended in the atmosphere, reported in aviation weather observations by type, amount, and height.
CLG: Calling — used in radiotelephony to indicate the act of establishing communication with a station, e.g., 'calling station'.
CLIMB-OUT: Climb-out area — the airspace area surrounding a departure path where terrain and obstacle clearance is assessed for aircraft during the initial climb phase after takeoff.
CLSD: Close or closed or closing — indicates that a runway, taxiway, airspace, facility, or portion thereof is not available for use.
CM: Centimetre — a unit of length in the metric system equal to one-hundredth of a metre, used in aviation for reporting runway conditions, visibility, and altimeter settings.
CMB: Climb to or climbing to — used in ATC clearances and NOTAMs to specify an instruction or intention to climb to a designated altitude or flight level.
COM: Communications — refers to voice and data link communication systems and services used in air traffic control and flight operations.
CONC: Concrete — a construction material used for runway, taxiway, and apron surfaces; reported in NOTAMs when surface conditions or work affect operations.
COND: Condition — used to describe the state or status of a facility, system, or surface, e.g., runway condition, braking condition.
CONS: Continuous — indicating an unbroken or uninterrupted operation, service, or condition, such as continuous broadcast of an aid or continuous weather phenomena.
CONST: Construction or constructed — indicates construction activity on or near an aerodrome facility that may affect aircraft operations, requiring NOTAM promulgation.
CONT: Continue(s) or continued — used in ATC instructions and NOTAMs to indicate the ongoing nature of a clearance, procedure, or condition.
COOR: Coordinate or coordination — the process of exchanging information and reaching agreement between air traffic control units or between ATC and other agencies.
COORD: Coordinates — a set of values (latitude and longitude) defining a precise geographic position, used in navigation, waypoints, and NOTAMs for locating hazards or facilities.
COP: Change-over point — a defined point along an airway or route at which an aircraft is expected to switch its primary navigation reference from the ground facility behind to the facility ahead.
COT: At the coast — a geographical reference indicating a location or condition along a coastline, used in NOTAMs and meteorological reports.
COV: Cover or covered or covering — used to describe the extent or presence of cloud cover, ice/snow coverage on surfaces, or the service coverage area of a navigation aid.
CRC: Cyclic redundancy check — an error-detecting code used in digital data communications to detect accidental changes to raw data, used in aviation data link systems.
CRM: Collision risk model — a mathematical model used to assess the probability of mid-air collisions, primarily applied in the separation standards for reduced lateral or vertical spacing.
CRP: Compulsory reporting point — a geographically defined point over which an aircraft must report its position to air traffic control, typically marked on aeronautical charts.
CRZ: Cruise — the phase of flight between climb and descent where the aircraft maintains a relatively constant altitude and airspeed for the en-route portion of the flight.
CS: Cirrostratus — a high-altitude cloud type forming a thin, whitish veil that often produces halos around the sun or moon, typically preceding warm frontal weather.
CTA: Control area — a designated airspace of defined dimensions within which air traffic control service is provided to IFR flights and, where applicable, VFR flights.
CTAM: Climb to and maintain — an ATC instruction directing an aircraft to climb to a specified altitude or flight level and then maintain that level.
CTC: Contact — used in aviation communications to mean establishing or maintaining radio communication with a specified station or facility.
CTL: Control — the authority or function of managing and directing aircraft movements, encompassing air traffic control, flight control, and ground control operations.
CTN: Caution — a warning term used in NOTAMs, ATC instructions, and aeronautical information to alert pilots to potential hazards or special conditions requiring attention.
CTR: Control zone — a controlled airspace extending upward from the surface to a specified upper limit around an aerodrome, designed to protect IFR traffic during approach and departure.
CU: Cumulus — a low-to-mid-level cloud type with a flat base and dense, fluffy tops, associated with fair weather or, when vertically developed, thunderstorms and precipitation.
CUF: Cumuliform — describing clouds having the characteristics of cumulus-type formations, i.e., with vertical development, distinct outlines, and a puffy or heaped appearance.
CUST: Customs — government agency responsible for regulating the import and export of goods; airport customs facilities are referenced in NOTAMs for international flight operations.
CVR: Cockpit voice recorder — a flight recorder that records the audio environment in the cockpit, including pilot conversations, ATC communications, and engine sounds, used for accident investigation.
CW: Continuous wave — a radio signal of constant amplitude and frequency, used in aviation for Morse code transmissions and as the basis for certain navigation aids such as NDBs.
CWY: Clearway — an area beyond the takeoff runway, under the control of the aerodrome operator, free of obstructions, which an aircraft may use during the initial climb for takeoff performance calculations.
D-VOLMET: Data link VOLMET — a digital data link service that provides en-route aircraft with meteorological information (METAR, TAF, SIGMET) via data link, supplementing traditional voice VOLMET broadcasts.
